newsitem.title: FRANCE: Details of French government welfare bill - table.
newsitem.headline: Details of French government welfare bill - table.

text.p: The French government gave the following details of its plans to reduce the welfare deficit next year to 29.7 billion francs from a forecast 47.15 billion next year, excluding new measures, and 51.6 billion this year
(savings and higher revenues in billions of francs)
Forecast excluding new measures -47.2
HEALTHCARE FUNDING REFORMS Ceiling on healthcare spending
(To be reduced to 600.2 bln Ffr from
604.5 billion francs this year) 3.5
Reform of payroll charges for healthcare 1.3
Increase in excise duties on alcohol 1.5
Increase in duties on tobacco 3.0
One-off contribution from Electricite de France
and Gaz de France following legal change on
transfer to state of EDF/GDF payroll charges 3.0
Transfer from army social security reserves 1.2
Transfer from funds for workplace accidents 1.0
REFORMS TO FAMILY BENEFITS
Reforms to housing aid 0.6
Changes to single parent allowances 0.15
REFORMS TO OLD-AGE BENEFITS AND PENSIONS
Transfer from special FSV funds 1.5
MEASURES COVERING ALL AREAS
End to tax break covering both early retirement
and part-time work for same employee 0.2
Reform to charges covering insurance when
company bankrupt or unable to pay wages 1.55
TOTAL NEW MEASURES 17.5
GOVERNMENT FORECAST DEFICIT 29.7
NOTES - Parliament is due to debate a bill on reforming social security financing on October 28 to 31.

The government said it intended to control health spending through the continuation of measures introduced in 1996 setting spending limits for doctors, through the distribution of compulsory individual medical records, a redistribution of funding between hospitals, encouragement of the use of generic medecines and early retirements of doctors between 56 and 65 years old.
The government's figures are rounded to the nearest hundred million, which may explain why figures given in the table do not add up to total.
The social security accounts commission earlier gave the following breakdown of its forecasts, excluding new measures, in billions of francs:
Health Care -39.7 -33.6 -31.2
Work Accidents 1.1 0.6 1.8
Family Benefits -38.9 -12.8 -8.7
Pensions 10.1 -5.8 -9.0
